pretreatments.description: Basic Pretreatment (BP) involves adding 2 N NaOH to the mixture to reach a pH of 12, followed by stirring at 70 rpm for 24 h at 30 ± 1 °C, and neutralizing with 2 N HCl before inoculum addition. This chemical treatment improves hydrolysis efficiency in ligno-cellulosic materials like OP through saponification reactions that increase porosity, reduce polymer degree of crystallinity, and disrupt structural links between lignin and carbohydrates.

Salt Pretreatments (SP) involve treating OP and OMWW mixtures with solid salts (FeSO_4, MnSO_4, FeCl_3, CaCO_3) to achieve a 5 g/L salt concentration. The process includes adding 2 N HCl to reach pH 2, adding the specific salt at desired concentration, holding at 70 rpm for 24 h, and neutralizing with 2 N NaOH. This chemical treatment includes FeSO_4, FeCl_3, MnSO_4, and CaCO_3 as distinct pretreatment conditions.

Dilution with Water (WP) involves adding tap water to the feed mixture to increase biogas production and methane content. This is a physical pretreatment that reduces acidity and polyphenol concentration in the reaction medium, though it has high lag phases (λ) and HPT due to slow kinetics.

Ultrasonic Pretreatment (USP) involves sonicating the mixture in an ultrasonic bath (CP823) at 30 °C, atmospheric pressure, and applying 1.8 kW of power for varying times (initially 8000 kJ/L for BMP, then 750 kJ/L for energy sustainability). This physical treatment breaks down complex molecular structures (lignin, cellulose) to increase surface area and mass transfer for microbial degradation.

Combined Pretreatment (USP + Salt) involves combining ultrasonic pretreatment (USP) with specific salt pretreatments (CaCO_3 or FeCl_3). For example, CP_Ca involves ultrasonic pretreatment followed by CaCO_3 treatment, and CP_FeIII involves ultrasonic pretreatment followed by FeCl_3 treatment. This combination aims to increase biogas production and efficiency.
